original.text: 子曰。學而時習之、不亦說乎。有朋自遠方來、不亦樂乎。人不知而不慍、不亦君子乎

variants.simplified: 子曰。学而时习之、不亦说乎。有朋自远方来、不亦乐乎。人不知而不愠、不亦君子乎

translations.text: The Master said: "Isn't it a pleasure to study and practice what you have learned? Isn't it also great when friends visit from distant places? If people do not recognize me and it doesn't bother me, am I not a noble man?"

commentary.text: One reading is that learning takes root through practice, while friendship brings its own joy. The final line shifts attention from public recognition toward a person's steadiness.

translations.text: You Zi said: “There are few who have developed themselves filially and fraternally who enjoy offending their superiors. Those who do not enjoy offending superiors are never troublemakers. The noble man concerns himself with the fundamentals. Once the fundamentals are established, the proper way appears. Are not filial piety and obedience to elders fundamental to the actualization of fundamental human goodness?”

commentary.text: One reading is that You Zi presents family relationships as a starting point for wider ethical life. The passage connects self-cultivation and respect for elders with benevolence; this describes the text's argument without treating every inherited hierarchy as unquestionable.
commentary.author: Mushroom Zi (AI-generated)

commentary.text: 有一種讀法是，有子把家庭中的孝悌視為更廣泛倫理生活的起點。篇章將修身與敬長連結到仁的實踐；這是在呈現文本的論述，並非要把所有傳統階序視為理所當然。
